title: Machine learning selects an exploratory senescence-related gene score in PMOS
summary: Using two public ovarian-cell datasets (13 PMOS and 9 control samples), univariate logistic regression, SVM-RFE and LASSO selected a five-gene SASP-related score (DYNLRB2, MMP9, A1BG, PGD, APLP2) with apparent AUC 0.991 on the development data and AUC 0.838 in an exploratory skeletal-muscle dataset (10 versus 13 samples). The authors state the apparent AUC should not be interpreted as evidence of diagnostic ability: dataset origin is confounded with cell type, the muscle dataset is not tissue-matched, no individual gene there remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and virtual screening against MMP9 is unvalidated. No laboratory experiments were reported.
ai_technology: Logistic regression, SVM-RFE and LASSO select a five-gene score from public transcriptomes; DrugCLIP screens compounds against MMP9 in silico.
organization: Seventh People's Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Changhai Hospital, Naval Medical University

evidence.tested: Five-gene score evaluated on the development data as an apparent AUC and on a non-tissue-matched skeletal-muscle dataset with fixed coefficients.
evidence.unknown: No independent tissue-matched validation; very small samples; no bootstrap or nested cross-validation; no comparator diseases; no experimental test.
evidence.ai_role: Logistic regression, SVM-RFE and LASSO selected the five genes forming the score.

source_review.scope: Frontiers article text read through abstract, datasets, methods, results and stated limitations (first 100,000 of about 170,000 characters); end of Discussion not read.
